extracted.intended_audience: photographers entering the World Press Photo Contest; jurors and contest stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative criteria for judging entries in the 2026 World Press Photo Contest, covering jury composition, rounds, information disclosure, and substantive criteria (visual quality, story, representation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual quality
rubrics_metrics.description: this can include creativity, technical skill and visual style, and the edit of the story (where relevant)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: World Press Photo asks the jury to consider visual quality while judging. Round 1 gives no photographer information specifically to ensure entries progressing are selected for their visual quality. Visual quality may cover creativity, technique, style and editing decisions for stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story
rubrics_metrics.description: this refers to the story and/or issues covered in the photographs, its relevance or significance, and the way in which the photographer has chosen to approach the story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges should assess the subject matter, the significance/relevance of the issues depicted, and the photographer's editorial/approach choices. For multi-image entries the edit and narrative treatment are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation
rubrics_metrics.description: this refers to the importance of awarding a diverse range of stories and photographers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization asks the jury to consider representation as part of judging. Specific representation targets are set (see separate metrics) to ensure diverse perspectives are represented across winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission-aligned standards (accuracy, authenticity, visual excellence, diverse perspectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: World Press Photo sets criteria to ensure the selection works towards the organization’s mission of promoting standards of accuracy, authenticity, visual excellence, while ensuring diverse perspectives are represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These high-level standards guide jurors without restricting their deliberations; jurors retain freedom to define what makes an entry award-worthy but should consider accuracy, authenticity and visual excellence alongside representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional jury initial selection
rubrics_metrics.description: In each of the six regions a selection of entries per category is first made by a regional jury composed of five professionals from and/or working in that region, with a range of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional juries use their knowledge of the region — including political, social and cultural understanding — to inform deliberations. Initial shortlisting per category is the responsibility of these regional juries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global jury final selection and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The global jury is composed of the six regional jury chairs and one additional member – the global jury chair. Once the regional juries have made their selection of entries, the global jury decides on 42 winners and from those entries, the World Press Photo of the Year is chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The global jury makes the final award decisions; the process is supported by non-voting staff/secretary (see secretary role).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary role and non-voting procedural neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: The secretary is responsible for all procedural matters and ensures the rules and procedures are fairly and properly applied. The secretary does not contribute to debate on the merits of any entry, and has no vote in the balloting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The secretary assists the global jury on procedures only. The secretary is supported by a jury coordinator (World Press Photo staff) who acts as the conduit of information; neither the coordinator nor other staff contribute to merit debate or voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff neutrality and logistical role
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the judging process, the role of World Press Photo staff is solely to manage the logistics of the judging process, including showing the entries, providing captions, and recording which entries are selected for the next round. No member of staff, including the jury coordinator, contributes to debate on the merits of any entry, and no member of staff has a vote in the balloting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff provide logistical support and information but remain neutral on merits to preserve independence of jury decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging rounds and voting process
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest has six voting rounds: the first, second, third, fourth and fifth rounds and the finals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The voting system and processes for each round are detailed in the Judging Procedures Handbook, which is provided to each juror and guides the judging process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information disclosure by round (anonymity and staged contextual information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Round 1: No photographer information given. From Round 2 onwards: The photographer’s nationality, where they are based, gender, title of the work and short caption is provided. From Round 3 onwards: The longer caption is provided. From Round 4 onwards: Individual photo captions, as well as additional information relating to how and why the story was made, such as motivation, the type of project (assignment/personal project) and funding is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographer names and other personal information not listed above are withheld throughout the judging process to preserve anonymity until winners are selected. The staged disclosure is designed so Round 1 selections are based on visual quality and later rounds allow more contextual assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation targets (at least one local winner per region)
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one local* winner per region
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit representation criterion intended to ensure regional/local voices are represented among winners. See local definition for who qualifies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation targets (gender diversity)
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one winner identifying as female or non-binary per region
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explicit per-region target to ensure gender diversity among winners; implemented alongside other representation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local photographer definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A photographer is considered local if they are from the country (and/or community) where the story is being covered – specifically, if they hold that country’s nationality or have lived and worked there for at least ten years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is applied to determine which winners count as 'local' for the regional representation requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of context, accountability, transparency and positionality
rubrics_metrics.description: The judging process emphasizes the importance of context and that means acknowledging accountability, transparency and positionality in image-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: World Press Photo provides juries with relevant information about the photographer at certain stages to facilitate a comprehensive approach to understanding and judging entries; jurors should consider these aspects when evaluating entries in later rounds.
